what_it_does: Large language models (LLMs) — AI systems that generate text — involve two broad categories of math: linear operations (huge matrix multiplications that current AI chips are optimized for) and nonlinear operations (functions like softmax, which converts a list of raw scores into probabilities; layer normalization, which rescales values to keep training stable; and others). These nonlinear functions are increasingly a bottleneck at inference time but are poorly served by chips built primarily for linear math. PICACHU plugs in a special reconfigurable chip — called a CGRA (Coarse-Grained Reconfigurable Array), essentially a grid of small programmable computing units that can be rewired in software for each different nonlinear function — alongside the main AI chip, so the two can work in parallel and each handle what it's best at.
